findings.title: CSV export request lacks authentication headers
findings.rationale: The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function uses a plain `fetch` call without any headers. If the server endpoint `/pulls/:prId/findings.csv` requires authentication (as most other endpoints in this service do), the request will fail with a 401/403. The existing `apiFetch` wrapper likely includes credentials (e.g., Authorization header), but it is not used here because the response is a Blob. This will break the export feature for any authenticated user.

findings.title: Client calls undefined endpoint
findings.rationale: The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function fetches from `/pulls/${prId}/findings.csv`, but no server route for this path is defined in the diff. Deploying this change will cause all CSV export attempts to fail with a 404 or 405 error, breaking the feature for every caller. The compatible alternative is to include the server-side implementation in the same PR, or to gate the client code behind a feature flag until the endpoint is deployed.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection in button onClick

If the fetch fails (e.g., network error, 404), the promise rejection will be unhandled, potentially causing a crash or silent failure. This does not break existing callers but degrades the user experience and makes debugging harder.

findings.title: Client-side contract copy not updated for new verdict
findings.rationale: The `Verdict` enum is defined in a shared contract that exists in two copies (server and client) that must be changed together. This PR only updates the server copy (line 26) to add `'needs_discussion'`. The client copy (expected at `client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts` or similar) remains unchanged, so any client that validates incoming verdicts against the old three-value enum will fail with a validation error when the server returns `needs_discussion`. This breaks all deployed callers that use the client-side contract, including the web client, e2e flows, and any external consumers.
